results.title: Foreign investors favor PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (EMAS) and PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI); Top 10 Net‑Buy Stocks of the Week
results.body: During the week of 14–18 September 2026, foreign investors recorded net purchases in ten Indonesian stocks, with PT Bumi Resources Minerals Tbk (BRMS), PT Merdeka Gold Resources Tbk (EMAS) and PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (AADI) leading the list. Net‑buy values were Rp324.7 billion for BRMS, Rp122.9 billion for EMAS, Rp115 billion for AADI, Rp92.3 billion for PT Amman Mineral Internasional Tbk (AMMN), Rp74.9 billion for PT Erajaya Swasembada Tbk (ERAA), Rp43.3 billion for PT Archi Indonesia Tbk (ARCI), Rp33.3 billion for PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (PGAS), Rp30.3 billion for PT Bukit Asam Tbk (PTBA), Rp28.9 billion for PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (ANTM) and Rp22 billion for PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk (TLKM). Overall foreign‑investor activity was a net sell of Rp1.84 trillion, coinciding with the IHSG index falling 1.53 % to 6,441,159, market‑capitalization decreasing 1.58 % to Rp11,266 trillion, and average daily transaction value, frequency and volume all declining. Analysts linked the market pressure to a 25‑basis‑point Fed rate hike to a 3.75‑4 % target range and expectations of further increases, which have been priced into the market.

results.title: Oil Price Upside Threatens to Boost MEDC, ELSA, PGAS and TPIA Stock Prospects
results.body: The article analyzes how a potential rise in global oil prices, driven by Iran‑U.S. geopolitical tension, could affect the stock prospects of four Indonesian energy companies. PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk is seen as the most positively impacted, with its upstream exposure, a projected production of 145 mboepd and a target price of Rp1,900 per share. PT Elnusa Tbk may benefit indirectly from higher upstream activity, supported by a Rp1.3 trillion contract backlog and a projected 12% YoY net‑profit growth, with a target price of Rp845; PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk is considered relatively defensive, backed by stable gas‑distribution volumes of 880 BBTUD and a target price of Rp1,615; while PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk faces mixed effects, with petrochemical spread expectations of US$350‑US$400 per ton, an additional US$120 million EBITDA from infrastructure assets, and a target price of Rp3,000. The analysts caution that if oil prices normalize to US$70‑US$80 per barrel, MEDC’s earnings would be most vulnerable, whereas ELSA and PGAS would remain comparatively defensive.

results.title: PGAS Loses Partial Arbitration Award, Ordered to Pay 9 LNG Cargoes to Gunvor
results.body: PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (PGAS) lost a partial arbitration award at the London Court of International Arbitration and must compensate Gunvor Singapore Pte Ltd with 9 LNG cargoes covering 2024 and 2025 deliveries. The partial award addresses Gunvor's claim for 4-8 cargoes in 2024 and 1-4 cargoes in 2025, while remaining claims for 2025 through 2027 are still pending. Gunvor reportedly claimed US$130.4 million (approximately Rp2.18 trillion) in the dispute, while PGAS provisioned US$72.02 million (approximately Rp1.2 trillion) in its December 2025 financial statements. The dispute stems from a 2022 master sales agreement for 8 cargoes annually through 2027, which PGAS declared force majeure on in November 2023. PGAS shares have fallen 18.59% year-to-date to Rp1,555.

results.title: PGAS Ordered to Pay Compensation to Gunvor Singapore After LCIA Arbitration Rejects Force Majeure Claim
results.body: Perusahaan Gas Negara (PGAS) must pay compensation to Gunvor Singapore following a partial award from the London Court of International Arbitration (LCIA) that rejected PGAS's force majeure declaration regarding LNG delivery obligations. The tribunal's decision covers nine LNG cargoes spanning cargoes 4-8 of 2024 and cargoes 1-4 of 2025, while reserving jurisdiction over remaining claims for 2025 through 2027 cargoes. Gunvor had previously claimed USD 130.4 million in the dispute arising from a master LNG sales and purchase agreement dated June 23, 2022, under which PGAS committed to deliver eight cargoes from January 2024 through December 2027. PGAS is currently conducting a comprehensive review with legal counsel Mayer Brown and relevant institutions to determine the impact and next steps. The award requires Gunvor to seek execution through the Central Jakarta District Court before enforcement.

results.title: PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk ordered to pay compensation to Gunvor Singapore after partial arbitration award
results.body: PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (PGAS) disclosed that a partial award (Arbitration No. 246358) from the London Court of International Arbitration requires it to pay compensation to Gunvor Singapore Pte. Ltd. The award was announced in a filing to the Indonesia Stock Exchange on 26 August 2026. Gunvor Singapore is the claimant in the arbitration, while PGAS is the respondent and listed issuer on the exchange. PGAS said it is conducting a thorough review of the partial decision and its implications for the company.

results.title: PGAS Ordered to Pay Compensation to Gunvor in LNG Arbitration Dispute
results.body: PGAS was ordered by the London Court of International Arbitration (case No. 246358) to pay compensation to Gunvor Singapore Pte Ltd over a liquefied natural gas (LNG) sales contract dispute. Gunvor’s claim amounts to US$130.4 million (approximately Rp2.18 trillion at Rp16,720/USD), while PGAS has set aside a provision of US$72.02 million (about Rp1.2 trillion) in its 2025‑2026 financial statements. The dispute stems from PGAS’s force‑majeure notice filed on 3 November 2023 that halted delivery of eight LNG cargoes scheduled between 1 January 2024 and 31 December 2027. PGAS’s shares have fallen 19.63 % this year to around Rp1,535, after reaching a high of Rp2,450 on 2 March 2026. The company may appeal the partial arbitration award in Indonesian courts.

results.title: IHSG predicted to trade sideways; MNC recommends ANTM, PGAS, PTBA, and TINS for Wednesday, 26 August 2026
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) will move sideways on Wednesday, 26 August 2026. It reports that IHSG closed at 6,501.6 on Monday, down 0.37%, with the property sector falling 1.67% and basic materials rising 1.38%, while the rupiah weakened to 17,712 per USD. Phintraco Sekuritas cites technical indicators—IHSG above its 100‑day moving average, a positive MACD histogram, and a Stochastic RSI near overbought—to support a sideways range of 6,450‑6,570. MNC Sekuritas warns of a short‑term correction between 6,429 and 6,453, targets 6,570‑6,600, and recommends the stocks ANTM, PGAS, PTBA, and TINS for trading on that day.

results.title: IHSG projected to strengthen at the start of the week
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia’s composite index (IHSG) will likely rise in early‑week trading. MNC Sekuritas analyst Herditya Wicaksana expects the index to move toward the 6,628‑6,666 range, testing the gap area while watching short‑term correction near 6,429‑6,475, and he recommends the stocks FORE, INCO, MBMA and TLKM. Binaartha Sekuritas analyst Ivan Rosanova sees a possible correction after the index failed to hold above the 6,545 resistance, targeting support around 6,441 and recommending JPFA, MDKA, PGAS and UNVR. The IHSG closed at 6,525 on Friday, up 24.10 points (0.37%) after a 1.93% weekly gain and trading volume of Rp17.42 trillion across 58.08 billion shares.

results.title: FTSE Russell’s September 2026 review reclassifies dozens of Indonesian stocks across Mid, Small and Micro Cap categories
results.body: FTSE Russell announced the results of its September 2026 semi‑annual review of the FTSE Global Equity Index Series, which reshuffled the classification of Indonesian equities. No changes occurred in the Large‑Cap segment, while PT Bumi Serpong Damai Tbk (BSDE) was removed from the Mid‑Cap index. Ten stocks left the Small‑Cap group and were largely transferred to Micro‑Cap, specifically BBYB, BJBR, BTPS, BSDE, LPKR, LPPF, MNCN, PNLF, SMRA and SCMA entered Micro‑Cap. Conversely, 27 stocks exited the Micro‑Cap category, including PT Resources Alam Indonesia Tbk, PT Bank Raya Indonesia Tbk, PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk and PT Steel Pipe Industry of Indonesia Tbk.

results.title: President Prabowo targets Rp200 trillion BUMN dividend by 2026 as state‑owned firms post strong 2025 profits
results.body: The article reports President Prabowo Subianto’s projection that state‑owned enterprises (BUMN) will remit a total dividend of Rp200 trillion to the state treasury by 2026, up from the Rp142.3 trillion paid in 2025. This outlook rests on the BUMN sector’s aggregate net profit of Rp326 trillion in 2025, a 75.3 % year‑on‑year increase from Rp186 trillion in 2024. Leading contributors include PT Bank Mandiri (Persero) Tbk. with profit of Rp30.41 trillion (+24.36 % YoY), PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk. with Rp15.49 trillion, PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk. with Rp10.76 trillion, PT Bank Tabungan Negara (Persero) Tbk. with Rp2.4 trillion, PT PP (Persero) Tbk. with Rp193,147 billion (+196.51 % YoY), PT Adhi Karya (Persero) Tbk. with Rp8.49 billion, PT Telkom Indonesia (Persero) Tbk. with Rp10.62 trillion, PT Dayamitra Telekomunikasi Tbk. with Rp1.11 trillion, and PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk. with US$90.45 million. The IDX BUMN 20 index has fallen 17.04 % year‑to‑date, outperforming the broader IHSG (‑25.41 %) and LQ45 (‑25.46 %), and analysts at KISI Securities suggest the index could outpace the market in the second half of 2026 if commodity prices stay high and MSCI re‑evaluation attracts foreign funds.

results.title: ENRG reports 27% profit rise to US$45.23 million, driven by sales to PLN and Pertamina
results.body: PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk (ENRG) posted a 27% year‑on‑year increase in net profit to US$45.23 million for the first half of 2026. Net sales grew 19% to US$283.37 million, with gas sales of US$163.36 million (57.65% of total) and oil sales accounting for 39.13% of revenue. Domestic sales were led by PT Pertamina Patra Niaga (US$43.19 million) and PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (US$67.41 million), while overseas sales went to TIS Petroleum (Asia) Pte. Ltd. (US$43.19 million). After the earnings release, ENRG’s shares opened about 4% higher, trading above Rp1,300 per share.

results.title: Energi Mega Persada posts net profit of Rp807.7 billion in the first half of 2026
results.body: PT Energi Mega Persada Tbk. (ENRG) reported a net profit of US$45.2 million (approximately Rp807.7 billion) for the first half of 2026. Revenue rose 18.51% year‑on‑year to US$283.37 million (about Rp5.05 trillion), driven by oil‑and‑gas sales of US$269.72 million, including US$163.3 million from natural gas and US$110 million from crude oil. Infrastructure sales contributed US$13.64 million, and the company’s major customers were TIS Petroleum (Asia) Pte. Ltd. (US$43.19 million), PT Pertamina Patra Niaga (US$92.25 million) and PT Perusahaan Listrik Negara (Persero) (US$67.41 million). CEO Syailendra S. Bakrie said the results reflect solid performance from existing assets and the firm will continue to optimise assets and pursue growth initiatives, while CFO Edoardus Ardianto emphasized maintaining financial flexibility.

results.title: Summary of Today's Stock Recommendations, 18 August 2026
results.body: The article provides a daily stock recommendation roundup for 18 August 2026. It notes that the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) closed at 6,401.88, down 0.12%, with a weekly low of 6,230.09 and a high of 6,462.7, while industrial stocks fell 5.14% and consumer stocks fell around 2% over the week. The recommended equities are BRI, HRTA, SRTG, INDY, BNI, BRPT, DSSA, CUAN, IATA, RAJA, TEBE, BMRI, BBNI, BBCA, TINS, MDKA, HMSP, DSNG, ADMR, AADI, ANTM, PGAS, VKTR, ARCI, INCO, WIIM, TLKM, SMGR, ITMG, PGEO, UNVR and INKP. These stocks are highlighted by securities firms including Danareksa Sekuritas, Phintraco Sekuritas, Phillip Sekuritas, MNC Sekuritas, CGS International Sekuritas, Panin Sekuritas, Mirae Asset Sekuritas and RHB Sekuritas. The market context shows a trading volume of 177.7 billion shares and a transaction value of Rp 76.17 trillion.

results.title: IHSG Likely to Brighten After Long Holiday as Analysts Forecast Upside and Recommend Select Stocks
results.body: The article forecasts that Indonesia’s composite stock index (IHSG) could continue its upward momentum after the recent long holiday. MNC Sekuritas analyst Herditya Wicaksana outlines best‑case targets of 6,440‑6,544 and worst‑case correction to 5,890‑6,192, with support at 6,201 and 6,029 and resistance at 6,454 and 6,599. Binaartha Sekuritas analyst Ivan Rosanova expects the index to break the internal resistance of 6,422 and aim for 6,545, citing support levels from 6,194 down to 5,887 and resistance up to 6,835. Both analysts recommend several equities, including AADI, ANTM, PGAS, VKTR, XMIG, ASII and BBNI, as potential beneficiaries of the projected rally. The index closed at 6,401 on 14 August, up 100.12 points (1.59 %) with trading volume of Rp12.44 trillion across 32.45 billion shares.

results.title: Foreign investors sell net Rp1.58 trillion of Indonesian stocks, top 10 net‑sell losers listed
results.body: Foreign investors recorded a net sell of Rp1.58 trillion in Indonesian equities from 10‑14 August 2026, with the biggest losers being PT Chandra Asri Pacific Tbk (Rp951.1 billion), PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp766.8 billion), PT Singaraja Putra Tbk (Rp455.7 billion), PT Astra International Tbk (Rp290.4 billion), PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (Rp238.7 billion), PT Indosat Tbk (Rp118.5 billion), PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp86.4 billion), PT Petrindo Jaya Kreasi Tbk (Rp73.4 billion), PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (Rp68.4 billion), PT Indo Tambangraya Megah Tbk (Rp66.2 billion), Kalbe Farma (Rp37.8 billion) and Darma Henwa (Rp35.9 billion). The outflows pressured the IHSG, which closed down 0.12 % at 6,401.89, while total market transactions fell 1.07 % to Rp15.21 trillion and trading volume dropped 14.86 % to 34.01 billion shares.

results.title: MNC Sekuritas projects IHSG to rise toward 6,544 and highlights gains in AADI, ANTM, PGAS, and VKTR
results.body: The article reports MNC Sekuritas' forecast that Indonesia's composite index (IHSG) could strengthen to the 6,440‑6,544 range. The index closed at 6,401, up 1.59%, with support at 6,201‑6,029 and resistance near 6,454‑6,599, and remains above the 20‑day moving average. The broker highlights that AADI rose 4.14% to 9,425, ANTM gained 2.33% to 3,070, PGAS increased 1.36% to 1,495, and VKTR jumped 7.93% to 885, each trading above MA20 and positioned in specific Elliott wave segments. Technical analysis suggests the index is in wave v of wave c, while the stocks are in various wave phases, indicating further upside potential.

results.title: RAPBN 2027’s expansive budget could lift a range of Indonesian stocks, according to RHB Sekuritas research
results.body: The article analyzes how the expansive 2027 state budget (RAPBN) may benefit specific Indonesian equities. RHB Sekuritas research expects the lower‑deficit, investment‑grade outlook and clearer project pipeline to support the Jakarta Composite Index (IHSG) and boost stocks in infrastructure, health, renewable energy, banking and commodities. Companies highlighted as potential winners include cement producers SMGR and INTP, contractors PTPP, ADHI and WIKA, health firms MIKA, HEAL, KLBF and SIDO, renewable‑energy and EV‑related firms PGEO, AUTO, TOBA, INDY and VKTR, major banks BMRI, BBNI, BBRI and BBCA, and commodity producers TINS, ANTM, INCO, PTBA, ITMG, ADRO, AALI, LSIP and TAPG. The budget also sets a Rp200 trillion dividend target for state‑owned enterprises, which could constrain retained earnings and capex for BUMN such as TLKM, PGAS, PTBA and ANTM, while tighter export rules may raise costs for some commodity exporters.

results.title: President Prabowo projects Indonesia’s state‑owned enterprises to pay Rp200 trillion in dividends by 2026 and highlights IDX High Dividend 20 BUMN stocks
results.body: President Prabowo projected that dividends from Indonesia’s state‑owned enterprises (BUMN) will reach Rp200 trillion in 2026 without any state capital injection (PMN). He noted that net dividend after PMN rose from Rp53 trillion in 2024 to Rp138 trillion in 2025, a 160 % increase, while total dividend grew from Rp53 trillion in 2024 to Rp142.3 trillion in 2025, a 67 % rise. The 2026 projection represents roughly a four‑fold increase over the 2024 level. The outlook highlights three BUMN constituents of the IDX High Dividend 20 index—PT Bank Negara Indonesia (Persero) Tbk., PT Bank Rakyat Indonesia (Persero) Tbk., and PT Perusahaan Gas Negara (Persero) Tbk.—as potential high‑dividend targets for investors.

results.title: Foreign investors net‑sell PT Bank Mandiri Tbk, PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk and other stocks as the IHSG rose 1.69%
results.body: The article reports that despite the IHSG gaining 1.69% to 6,373.84 points on 12 August 2026, foreign investors recorded net sales in several Indonesian equities. The biggest net‑sell positions were in PT Bank Mandiri Tbk (Rp 245.71 billion) and PT Telkom Indonesia Tbk (Rp 98.39 billion), followed by PT Medco Energi Internasional Tbk (Rp 30.96 billion), PT United Tractors Tbk (Rp 27.94 billion), PT Merdeka Copper Gold Tbk (Rp 25.39 billion), PT Aneka Tambang Tbk (Rp 24.88 billion), PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk (Rp 19.44 billion), PT Kalbe Farma Tbk (Rp 19.32 billion), PT Adaro Andalan Indonesia Tbk (Rp 17.38 billion) and PT Karya Pacific Energy Tbk (Rp 16.55 billion). Overall foreign investors posted a net buy jumbo of Rp 725.40 billion across the market, with 452 stocks advancing, 175 declining and 168 unchanged. The net‑sell activity highlights selective profit‑taking by foreigners even as the broader market rallied.

results.title: Foreign investors net sell BMRI, TLKM, MEDC and PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk amid IHSG gain
results.body: Foreign investors recorded net selling of several Indonesian stocks on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, with the most significant outflows in BMRI, TLKM, MEDC and PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk. Net sell totals were Rp 245.7 billion for BMRI, Rp 98.3 billion for TLKM, Rp 30.9 billion for MEDC and Rp 19.4 billion for PT Perusahaan Gas Negara Tbk. Despite the outflows, foreign investors posted a net purchase of Rp 725.4 billion across the market, including Rp 482.7 billion in the regular market and Rp 242.6 billion in the negotiation and cash segments, while the IHSG closed up 105.97 points (1.69%) at 6,373.8. Overall trading volume reached Rp 17.3 trillion, with 474 stocks advancing, 185 declining and 304 remaining unchanged.
